meta.title: My rough classification of the ICML 2026 papers
meta.dek: I was going through the ICML 2026 program in Seoul and roughly classified the papers I read. The shape I kept seeing: the model is increasingly its own teacher — self-play, self-reward, self-correction and self-evolving memory move from tricks to training regimes.
meta.meta_html: Scope: self-improvement, reasoning, agents, retrieval & ranking, RL/RLHF, efficiency, generation, evaluation & theory  |  a curated, verified sample — not the full 6,600+  |  ↗ Reading list

takeaway: My overall read: the center of gravity this year is self-improvement. The interesting question stopped being “how do we supervise the model” and became “how does the model supervise itself” — and, one level up, how does it evolve the machinery (memory, verifier, reward) that does the supervising.
shifts_heading: Roughly, the papers fell into these groups

shifts.heading: Agents that rewrite themselves
shifts.prose: The headline shift: agents that improve by editing their own experience, memory, or policy rather than by another round of human fine-tuning. Several papers push past agent-level tuning to meta-evolution — evolving the memory architecture itself, not just its contents. The sharpest open question is faithfulness: at least one paper shows these self-evolvers can drift or deceive themselves, so “it improved on the benchmark” is not yet “it improved.”

anchors.title: MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems
Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
From Interactions to Principles: Experience-Driven Self-Distillation for Evolving LLM Agents

shifts.heading: Self-play is back, and it is aimed at code
shifts.prose: Self-play returned as a serious training signal, now pointed at software engineering and quantitative reasoning rather than board games. The recurring recipe is a single model that both proposes a challenge (inject a bug, set a market) and solves it, with an anchor or reference set to stop the two halves drifting into an unrealistic private language.

anchors.title: Toward Training Superintelligent Software Agents through Self-Play SWE-RL
Evolving Quantitative Reasoning through Self-Play in Digital Twin Markets

shifts.heading: Reward without humans: self-reward, self-consistency, weak verification
shifts.prose: A cluster on where the reward comes from when nobody labels anything. Some turn self-supervised objectives into dense verifiable rewards; some let the model meta-evaluate its own outputs; and a theory strand asks when a cheap self-check (self-consistency, a proxy reward) is actually good enough to trust versus when you need a strong verifier.

anchors.title: Conversation for Non-verifiable Learning: Self-Evolving LLMs through Meta-Evaluation
SSL4RL: Revisiting Self-supervised Learning as Intrinsic Reward for Visual-Language Reasoning
When to Trust the Cheap Check: Weak and Strong Verification for Reasoning

shifts.heading: Test-time RL and self-correction as first-class training
shifts.prose: Correction moved from a decoding trick to an objective you train against. Test-time RL updates the policy from self-generated pseudo-labels at inference; multi-attempt training rewards a model for fixing its own earlier answer. The tension is reward hacking — self-generated labels are exactly the ones a model is biased to agree with.

anchors.title: Beyond Majority Voting: Self-Reflective Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
Learning to Correct: Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Attempt Chain-of-Thought

shifts.heading: The judge problem gets quantified
shifts.prose: As evaluation leans on LLM-as-judge, the papers stopped assuming the judge is neutral and started modelling its reliability — per-judge discriminators, judge-aware ranking, and direct measurement of judge bias. If you are going to reward a model with another model, this is the load-bearing wall.

anchors.title: A Judge-Aware Ranking Framework for Evaluating LLMs without Ground Truth
Who can we trust? LLM-as-a-jury for Comparative Assessment

shifts.heading: Retrieval learns to reason — and to act
shifts.prose: Retrieval stopped being a fixed first stage. Reasoning-intensive retrievers and rerankers are trained to think before they rank, and deep-research agents optimise the whole search loop end-to-end with RL. The open question is cost: agentic, multi-turn retrieval is powerful but expensive, so a parallel push shrinks the encoders and prunes the reranking.

anchors.title: DR Tulu: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics for Deep Research
Graph-R1: Towards Agentic GraphRAG Framework via End-to-end Reinforcement Learning
ModernVBERT: Towards Smaller Visual Document Retrievers

thread.heading: One quieter thread: the generative-modelling theory kept its edge
thread.html: Away from the agent noise, the diffusion/flow-matching theory was some of the sharpest work — two of the Outstanding Paper awards went here: High-Accuracy Sampling for Diffusion Models and Log-Concave Distributions ICML (arXiv) and The Flexibility Trap: Rethinking the Value of Arbitrary Order in Diffusion Language Models ICML, the latter a useful cold-shower on arbitrary-order generation.

appendix_title: The full list, grouped the way I sorted it
appendix_dek: The ICML 2026 papers I went through, each with a one-line note and its ICML program link (arXiv where I could verify a preprint). This is a curated sample, not the whole proceedings.

papers.title: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents
papers.note: A GUI agent that pairs hierarchical memory with an iterative self-improvement pipeline (test-time memory extension plus memory-augmented self-evolution training).

papers.title: Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
papers.note: Shows self-evolving agents that reuse past experience can fail to faithfully reflect it — a caution on trusting self-reported improvement.

papers.title: From Interactions to Principles: Experience-Driven Self-Distillation for Evolving LLM Agents
papers.note: EvolveR distills an agent's own interaction history into reusable strategic principles and feeds them back via self-distillation.

papers.title: On the Generalization Gap in Self-Evolving Language Model Reasoning
papers.note: Measures how far self-generated supervision sits from oracle supervision across four self-evolution methods on controlled logical reasoning.

papers.title: MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems
papers.note: Jointly evolves an agent's experiential knowledge and its memory architecture, so the system improves how it learns, not just what it knows.

papers.title: Toward Training Superintelligent Software Agents through Self-Play SWE-RL
papers.note: One LLM trained by RL self-play to inject and repair increasingly hard bugs specified by test-suite improvements; beats a human-data baseline on SWE-bench.

papers.title: Anchoring Self-Play for Code Repair
papers.note: Generator-fixer self-play in a single model, anchored to a reference set so injected bugs stay close to real-world ones.

papers.title: Evolving Quantitative Reasoning through Self-Play in Digital Twin Markets
papers.note: Agents test and adapt strategies via self-play in a controllable digital-twin market, forming a bounded self-evolving loop.

papers.title: Conversation for Non-verifiable Learning: Self-Evolving LLMs through Meta-Evaluation
papers.note: CoNL unifies generation, evaluation and meta-evaluation via multi-agent self-play, beating self-rewarding baselines without external judges.

papers.title: SSL4RL: Revisiting Self-supervised Learning as Intrinsic Reward for Visual-Language Reasoning
papers.note: Turns self-supervised objectives into dense, automatic, verifiable rewards for RL fine-tuning — no human preferences or AI judges.

papers.title: When to Trust the Cheap Check: Weak and Strong Verification for Reasoning
papers.note: Analyzes when weak verification (self-consistency, proxy rewards) suffices versus when a strong verifier is required.

papers.title: Optimal Self-Consistency for Efficient Reasoning with Large Language Models
papers.note: Derives power-law scaling for self-consistency and analyzes fixed- versus dynamic-allocation sampling for chain-of-thought.

papers.title: Beyond Majority Voting: Self-Reflective Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
papers.note: SR-TTRL uses self-reflective verification to produce high-fidelity pseudo-labels for test-time RL instead of majority voting.

papers.title: Learning to Correct: Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Attempt Chain-of-Thought
papers.note: Trains reasoning models to make multiple verified attempts with self-reflection, improving self-correction over long chains.

papers.title: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for Flow Matching
papers.note: Flow-TTRL aligns text-to-image generation on the fly by reinterpreting intermediate latents as an implicit policy.

papers.title: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning
papers.note: Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning learns on-policy directly from demonstrations, supporting continual learning without catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.note: OPSD has one LLM act as both teacher and student under different contexts to improve reasoning.

papers.title: AsyncSpade: Efficient Test-Time Scaling with Asynchronous Sparse Decoding
papers.note: Cuts the KV-cache bottleneck of long chain-of-thought test-time scaling with asynchronous sparse decoding, >20% faster per token at matched accuracy.

papers.title: UniScale: Adaptive Unified Inference Scaling via Online Joint Optimization of Model Routing and Test-Time Scaling
papers.note: Casts model routing plus test-time scaling as a contextual bandit over the quality-cost trade-off.

papers.title: HERMES: Towards Efficient and Verifiable Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
papers.note: A tool-assisted agent interleaving informal reasoning with formally verified Lean proofs, raising accuracy while spending fewer tokens.

papers.title: Multi²: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Decision-Making with LLM-Based Agents in Interactive Environments
papers.note: Decomposes agent behavior into complementary hierarchical roles for decision-making in interactive environments.

papers.title: AgentNoiseBench: Benchmarking Robustness of Tool-Using LLM Agents Under Noisy Conditions
papers.note: Systematically evaluates tool-using agents under both user-side instruction noise and tool-side result noise.

papers.title: SciAgentGym: Benchmarking Multi-Step Scientific Tool-Use in LLM Agents
papers.note: A scalable environment with 1,780 domain tools across four natural sciences plus a tiered agentic tool-use benchmark.

papers.title: AppWorld-UL: Benchmarking Diverse Agent-User Interactions for Tool-Use
papers.note: 306 user-in-the-loop tasks needing diverse agent-user interaction across nine simulated apps.

papers.title: ExCyTIn-Bench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Cyber Threat Investigation
papers.note: Evaluates agents on cyber threat investigation using questions derived from investigation graphs.

papers.title: Rethinking the Reranker: Boundary-Aware Evidence Selection for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.note: BAR-RAG reframes the RAG reranker as a boundary-aware evidence selector targeting the generator's usable zone, ~10% end-to-end QA gain under noisy retrieval.

papers.title: Very Efficient Listwise Multimodal Reranking for Long Documents
papers.note: ZipRerank shortens input via query-image early interaction and scores all candidates in one forward pass, up to 10x lower reranking latency on MMDocIR.

papers.title: Ranking Free RAG: Replacing Re-ranking with Selection in RAG for Sensitive Domains
papers.note: METEORA swaps relevance re-ranking for rationale-driven evidence selection with an elbow-detection cutoff and a verifier LLM, more accurate with fewer chunks.

papers.title: DR Tulu: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics for Deep Research
papers.note: An open long-form deep-research agent trained with rubrics that co-evolve with the policy to give discriminative on-policy feedback.

papers.title: DECOR: Learning to Decompose and Collaborate in Deep Search via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.note: Multi-agent RL that decomposes deep-search tasks and coordinates collaborating agents on complex information-seeking queries.

papers.title: Graph-R1: Towards Agentic GraphRAG Framework via End-to-end Reinforcement Learning
papers.note: Builds a lightweight knowledge hypergraph and models retrieval as multi-turn agent-environment interaction, optimised end-to-end with RL.

papers.title: From Conflict to Consensus: Boosting Medical Reasoning via Multi-Round Agentic RAG
papers.note: MA-RAG turns semantic conflict among candidate answers into new retrieval queries across agentic rounds for medical QA.

papers.title: HypRAG: Hyperbolic Dense Retrieval for Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.note: Hyperbolic dense retrievers in Lorentz space with geometry-aware pooling, beating Euclidean baselines on MTEB and RAGBench.

papers.title: AOEB: Benchmarking Agent-Oriented Multimodal Embeddings
papers.note: A multi-task multimodal embedding benchmark for agent-centric retrieval (code, tool, reasoning, memory) beyond MTEB.

papers.title: ModernVBERT: Towards Smaller Visual Document Retrievers
papers.note: A 250M-parameter vision-language encoder for visual document retrieval that matches models up to 10x larger, CPU-efficient.

papers.title: Multi-Objective Preference Optimization: Improving Human Alignment of Generative Models
papers.note: MOPO maximizes a primary preference objective under tunable lower bounds on secondary objectives via KL-regularized constraints.

papers.title: Reliability-Aware LLM Alignment from Inconsistent Human Feedback
papers.note: Tackles DPO's tendency to overfit ambiguous, high-disagreement preference pairs by modelling annotator reliability.

papers.title: Autoregressive Direct Preference Optimization
papers.note: ADPO folds autoregressive structure explicitly into the DPO objective.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback
papers.note: Distributionally robust formulations for both reward-based RLHF and reward-free DPO.

papers.title: Advantage Collapse in Group Relative Policy Optimization: Diagnosis and Mitigation
papers.note: Diagnoses and mitigates advantage-collapse failure modes in GRPO-style RL fine-tuning.

papers.title: Vegas: Self-Speculative Decoding with Verification-Guided Sparse Attention
papers.note: Identifies critical KV entries as a byproduct of verification and loads only those when drafting subsequent tokens.

papers.title: SoftMoE: Soft Differentiable Routing for Mixture-of-Experts in LLMs
papers.note: Replaces discrete MoE routing with a truncated soft top-k relaxation, enabling gradient-based routing while activating fewer experts.

papers.title: ReMoE: Boosting Expert Reuse through Router Fine-Tuning in Memory-Constrained MoE Inference
papers.note: Router fine-tuning to raise token-wise expert reuse for fine-grained MoE under memory-constrained inference.

papers.title: Mean Flow Distillation: Robust and Stable Distillation for Flow Matching Models
papers.note: A stable distillation method for flow-matching models, SoTA on 4D occupancy forecasting and text-to-image.

papers.title: High-Accuracy Sampling for Diffusion Models and Log-Concave Distributions
papers.note: Outstanding Paper: training-free first-order rejection sampling giving polylog(1/δ)-step high-accuracy diffusion sampling from scores alone.

papers.title: The Flexibility Trap: Rethinking the Value of Arbitrary Order in Diffusion Language Models
papers.note: Outstanding Paper questioning whether arbitrary generation order actually helps diffusion language models.

papers.title: A Kinetic-Energy Perspective of Flow Matching
papers.note: Introduces Kinetic Path Energy, an action-like diagnostic of accumulated effort along a flow ODE trajectory.

papers.title: A Judge-Aware Ranking Framework for Evaluating LLMs without Ground Truth
papers.note: Improves human-preference agreement in ground-truth-free evaluation by modelling judge reliability and calibrating ranking uncertainty.

papers.title: Who can we trust? LLM-as-a-jury for Comparative Assessment
papers.note: A Bradley-Terry extension with per-judge discriminator parameters to jointly infer rankings and judge reliability.

papers.title: Quantifying Biases in LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluations
papers.note: Systematically measures biases in LLM-as-a-judge autograders used as a scalable stand-in for human evaluation.

papers.title: QEDBench: Quantifying the Alignment Gap in Automated Evaluation of University-Level Mathematical Proofs
papers.note: First benchmark contrasting course rubrics with expert criteria for grading undergraduate math proofs.

papers.title: MultiBreak: A Scalable and Diverse Multi-turn Jailbreak Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Safety
papers.note: 10,389 adversarial prompts spanning 2,665 distinct harmful intents for multi-turn jailbreak evaluation.

papers.title: Steering Beyond the Support: Adversarial Training on Unsupervised Jailbroken Activation Simulation
papers.note: A bi-level adversarial training scheme for zero-shot jailbreak defense, mostly <5% attack success across three LLMs.

papers.title: Jailbreak Foundry: From Papers to Runnable Attacks for Reproducible Benchmarking
papers.note: A multi-agent system that turns published jailbreak papers into executable attack modules for reproducible safety benchmarks.

papers.title: LALM-as-a-Judge: Benchmarking Large Audio-Language Models for Safety Evaluation in Multi-Turn Spoken Dialogues
papers.note: Benchmarks large audio-language models as safety judges in multi-turn spoken dialogue.

papers.title: Generalization and Scaling Laws for Mixture-of-Experts Transformers
papers.note: A generalization/scaling theory for MoE Transformers that separates active per-input capacity from routing combinatorics.

papers.title: Understanding Generalization and Forgetting in In-Context Continual Learning
papers.note: Extends single-task in-context-learning theory to task sequences to characterize generalization and forgetting.

papers.title: Dynamics and representation structure of local approximations to gradient-based learning in linear recurrent neural networks
papers.note: Uses dynamical-systems theory on data-aligned linear RNNs to compare stability and convergence of local gradient approximations.

sources_html: ICML 2026 program (Seoul, July 6–11): accepted papers via icml.cc/virtual/2026 · awards via the ICML 2026 awards blog · preprints on arXiv where verified.
method_html: How I built this: I read across the ICML 2026 program and sorted a curated sample into the buckets above, weighting the self-improvement clusters because that was the year's throughline. This is not a complete pass — ICML 2026 accepted 6,600+ papers and I covered a fraction. Every paper here was checked against its icml.cc/virtual/2026 program page (which confirms the exact title and venue); ICML publishes through OpenReview/PMLR rather than assigning DOIs, so the link chip points at the program page, with arXiv added only where I could match a preprint. Nothing here is a guessed link.
footer_onepager: Every paper cited links to its ICML 2026 program page (arXiv where a preprint was verified). Full annotated appendix follows.
footer_appendix: Prepared July 2026. A curated, verified sample of ICML 2026 — not the complete proceedings.
